title: Dissection of murine collecting lymphatic vessels for imaging, single-cell analysis, and tissue culture of lymphatic muscle cells
protocol: Anesthetize mouse using an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine/xylazine cocktail.
Wait until the mouse does not react to a toe pinch.
Remove fur from hindlimbs using mechanical clippers.
Apply hair removal cream for 30 seconds using a cotton tip applicator.
Wipe away the hair removal cream with a paper towel wetted with water.
Dry the area after removing the cream.
Inject 2% Evans blue subcutaneously in the foot pad of both limbs.
Pull skin flap to expose vessels.
Cut skin flap to reveal vessels.
Pull upwards on fat layer covering vascular branch.
Pull downwards on fat layer covering vascular branch.
Inject between digital and metatarsal pads at middle point of paw back with a volume of 10-20 μL using insulin syringe containing 28G × ½ inch needle.
Place mouse in lid of sterile Petri dish in prone position.
Tape ankle and upper part of thigh to immobilize surgical area.
Sanitize surgical area with iodine and alcohol wipes.
Remove the skin from the hind limb of the mouse to expose the vessels in the ankle area.
Place the mouse in the orientation as depicted for procedures involving PLV exposure.
Use a stereomicroscope to assist in removing the skin and underlying connective tissue.
Locate the popliteal lymphatic vessel (PLVs) in the ankle area through the skin after Evans blue injection into the footpad.
Pinch a portion of the skin without PLVs using blunt forceps on one side of the ankle.
Make a cut with micro scissors where the skin is pinched and repeat this procedure on the other side.
Extend both cuts laterally towards the end of the thigh, using the blood vessel as a reference point.
Once the end of the thigh is reached, make a transverse cut to join the lateral incisions.
Pull downwards to expose the popliteal lymphatic vessels (PLVs) and blood vessels (BVs).
Cut the skin flap to reveal the vessels from the lymph node to the ankle.
Remove any blood coming from broken capillaries using a sterile cotton applicator.
Hydrate the area with sterile PBS immediately after removing blood.
Use sterile PBS to keep the exposed area hydrated during surgery.
Improve visibility of surrounding fat by adding sterile PBS.
Extract the membrane of fat covering the vessels using fine forceps and micro scissors.
Pull the membrane with fine forceps carefully.
Make small incisions in the fat using micro scissors or microscalpel.
Cut a section parallel to either the plantaris muscle lateral vessel (PLV).
Use micro scissors to cut the fat below the vascular branch from one side of the PLV to the other.
Extend separation of the vascular branch from underlying tissue with micro scissors.
Make two cuts with micro scissors to extract the vascular branch.
Pull the fat on the exterior side of the PLV upwards to aid in separation.
Trim the fat surrounding the vessels once a cut has been made on the side of the PLV.
Continue cutting until the three vessels are separated from the underlying tissue.
Cut from the other side of the vascular branch if necessary.
Widen the separation area with a microscalpel or micro scissors as needed.
Retrieve the area of interest using micro scissors after it is separated from the fat and BV.
Place in PBS to wash off blood.
Place in 4% PFA for 1–4 h at 18°C–25°C.
Wash with PBS for at least 1 h at 18°C–25°C or overnight at 4°C.
Follow an appropriate protocol for OCT (cryosections) or paraffin embedding for sectioning.
Permeate samples with 0.5% triton (in PBS) at 4°C for 12–14 hours in a microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate samples with PBS-glycine wash buffer for 20 minutes at 18°C–25°C.
Repeat the PBS-glycine wash three times, each for 20 minutes.
Incubate samples with blocking buffer (10% normal donkey serum in immunofluorescence wash buffer) for 1 hour at 18°C–25°C.
Incubate samples with primary antibody for 24–48 hours at 4°C.
Wash three times with PBS, each for 20 minutes.
Incubate samples with secondary antibody (anti-goat 647 for Prox1) diluted 1:100 for 12–14 hours at 4°C.
Rinse samples with PBS for 20 minutes.
Repeat the PBS rinse three times.
Place the stained sample on a glass slide with enough PBS for hydration.
Use a glass coverslip to flatten tissue for imaging.
Cut the fat between one of the PLVs and the BV using fine forceps and micro scissors.
Use a stereomicroscope for better visualization during separation.
Pull on the PLV to initiate separation from surrounding tissue.
Separate PLV from BV by pulling and using the tip of the scalpel in a downward motion.
Progressively cut fat side to side with a scalpel to remove fat around LV.
Start with the PLV most distal from the BV.
Pull the fat adjacent to either PLV.
Make a small downward incision in the fat between the PLV and BV with the tip of a microscalpel.
Repeat until the PLV is completely separated from the underlying tissue.
Cut the fat on the exterior side of the PLV with micro scissors if necessary.
Be gentle when pulling the PLV to avoid slicing through the BV.
Widen the interior incision with the aid of the microscalpel or micro scissors.
Continue the process from the pLN ideally all the way down to the ankle, at least until reaching the vascular bend.
Perform step 27b in areas along the vessels that have high amounts of fat.
Rotate the Petri dish to work more comfortably on the other PLV.
Detach the BV before the PLV.
Cut the PLV with micro scissors and place in a 35 mm TC dish containing HBSS on ice.
Make the initial cut proximal to the pLN and then pull towards the ankle.
Apply an EtOH pad to stop bleeding when cutting the BV.
Separate the BV from the fat in the same way as the PLV.
Perform this section if a single cell suspension is required for downstream analysis.
Take the enzymatic solution from 37°C incubation and pipette 200 μL to the lid of the 35 mm TC plate.
Using fine forceps, transport the extracted LVs to the 200 μL of enzymatic solution.
With a P1000 pipette, transfer the enzymatic solution containing the vessels to a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube with the remainder of the enzymatic solution.
If the vessels do not dislodge easily, use forceps and micro scissors to detach them and transport them back to the lid.
Repeat this step if any vessels remain.
Incubate enzyme solution with vessels in a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 60 min.
Add 10 mL of DMEM with 10% FBS to neutralize enzymatic activity and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min.
Repeat the previous step twice.
Resuspend cell pellet in cell culture media (DMEM, 20% FBS, 1% P/S).
Take 10 μL of each cell solution for counting and assessing cell viability.
Add cell suspension from LVs and BVs to respective collagen-coated wells.
Grow cells in the cell culture incubator for 7 days.
Replace media after 5 days of plating to replenish nutrients.
Check cells every day to assess growth and potential microbial contamination.
